items.name: silent_error_pattern_critic
items.description: Add critic check that flags the logger.error(..., extra={'error': str(e)}) pattern (and siblings). When the root logger uses the default format, extra= fields are dropped silently, so the real exception message is invisible. SimbliClient.get_meetings used this pattern and hid 'Playwright Sync API inside the asyncio loop' for 42 minutes until we switched to logger.exception. Grep the codebase for other instances and either update or at least document the ban. Easiest home: .critics/silent-failure.critic.md or a new .critics/logging.critic.md.
items.notes: Filed 2026-04-20. Preventative: turns a latent 42-min discovery into a commit-time flag. One of three meta-learnings from simbli_incapsula_bypass. ~30 min to write the critic rule + grep for existing instances.

items.name: regional_server_deployment
items.description: Deploy bay-area.civicosproject.org/mcp (or marin.civicosproject.org/mcp) as an operational boundary separate from the per-city servers. It's literally the same codebase with CIVICOS_JURISDICTION and CIVICOS_REGION env vars pointing at the region, and a different Modal app name / Cloudflare subdomain. Users install ONE connector for regional coverage instead of N per-city connectors.
items.notes:
Depends on region_config_concept. Once regions are a first-class concept in the registry, deploying a new regional server is just a matter of (1) registering the new Modal app name in registry.json, (2) setting CIVICOS_REGION in a new Modal secret, (3) running modal deploy with CIVICOS_JURISDICTION set to a 'primary' jurisdiction in the region (likely county-marin or similar — needed for the open-tier fallback and for writes). May want to introduce a 'regional facade' jurisdiction type that explicitly has no writes — writes get refused with 'please use the connector for {city} to take this action'. Cloudflare DNS + Worker routing setup required (same pattern as existing subdomains). Not a blocker for shipping scope work — the per-city servers become regionally-capable after steps 1-3, so this is only needed for the clean 'one connector per region' UX.

items.name: fix_decision_storage_dedup
items.description: Decisions table accumulated duplicates because decision IDs were derived from the LLM's enumeration order (`decision:{jur}:{meeting_id}:{ordinal}`), which is non-deterministic across re-extractions and even within a single extraction when the LLM lists the same decision twice. Fixed by deriving IDs from a SHA-256 hash of LLM-stable fields (item_ref, title, item_type, outcome, budget_amount) so the temporal-versioning UPDATE in store_decisions() correctly matches prior versions across runs.
items.source: Phase B cross-county query validation finding
items.notes: Resolved 2026-04-07. The handoff hypothesis (4x affordable-housing rows in Berkeley as smoking gun) was MISDIAGNOSED — those 4 rows are 4 legitimately distinct housing-project decisions (North Berkeley BART, Ephesian Legacy Court, People's Park, Ashby Lofts) with identical generic LLM titles but distinct agenda_items. Same for SF's '5 identical AHSC' — 4 different meetings + 1 meeting with two sub-items. Real bug scope was much smaller: 8 actual same-run LLM duplications across 3 jurisdictions (county-alameda 6, city-novato 1, city-san-francisco 1). Cleanup applied via scripts/cleanup_decision_dedup.py (uses the same compute_stable_decision_id hash as the forward fix to guarantee consistency — zero false positives). Cross-county verification (scripts/verify_cross_county_phase_b.py) ALL CHECKS PASS post-fix. 21 unit tests + 4 integration tests added (test_integration_decision_dedup.py is the regression guard — reordered batch test is the exact bug repro). Forward fix prevents both re-extraction and same-run duplication causes. Follow-up: add_real_source_item_id to thread platform-stable IDs through extractors (P3).

items.name: add_real_source_item_id
items.description: Thread a real source-platform item ID (Granicus / Legistar / BoardDocs internal ID) through the extraction dataclass and storage so the stable decision ID can be derived from a true platform-stable reference instead of the synthetic-D fields (item_type, outcome, budget_amount). Today's fix uses the synthetic-D from already-available HighStakesDecision fields, which is sufficient but theoretically less robust if two genuinely-distinct decisions in one meeting share all of (item_ref, title, item_type, outcome, budget). Adds source_item_id: Optional[str] to HighStakesDecision and updates Granicus/Legistar/BoardDocs clients to populate it where the platform exposes one. Hash function adds source_item_id to the key when present.
items.notes: Filed 2026-04-07. The fix_decision_storage_dedup work shipped with synthetic-D (item_type + outcome + budget_amount as additional disambiguators) because real-D would have required threading a platform source ID through 3+ extractors, expanding the P0 scope significantly. Synthetic-D works in practice for current data but the LLM produces decisions from PDF text and has no view of platform-internal IDs — a real source ID would be ground-truth. Defer until either (a) we observe a synthetic-D collision in production, or (b) we onboard a city where this matters.

items.name: fix_sf_county_parent

items.name: upcoming_verb_ignores_jurisdiction
items.description: execute_upcoming() at packages/civicos-services/src/civicos_services/query/verbs.py line ~640 calls civic.whats_next(days=...) which uses civic.jurisdiction (the CivicOS instance attribute set at construction) rather than the explicit jurisdiction parameter passed into the verb. Same pattern repeats for the hearings and comment_periods event types in the same function. Effect: cross-jurisdiction fan-out routes upcoming queries to the wrong jurisdiction whenever a single CivicOS instance is reused across multiple jurisdiction calls. Discovered during mass-ingest validation pass on 2026-04-07: a shared-instance validation script returned san-rafael's upcoming events for tiburon, county-marin, county-alameda, and city-belvedere queries (all reported the same 'Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee' top result).
items.notes: Fix: thread `jid` through to a per-call jurisdiction-aware whats_next() (e.g., add a jurisdiction kwarg to CivicOS.whats_next or call the storage backend directly). Add a regression test that constructs ONE CivicOS(jid_a) and calls execute_upcoming(req, civic, jid_b) — the result must reflect jid_b's events, not jid_a's. Search request handlers already accept per-call jurisdiction correctly (verified during the same validation pass), so this is upcoming-specific. Severity: silent failure with no error — returned data looks plausible. Easy to miss in single-jurisdiction usage but catastrophic for federation/cross-jurisdiction routing.

items.name: decisions_adapter_crashes_on_empty_vectors
items.description: DecisionsAdapter.search() at packages/civicos-services/src/civicos_services/query/adapters.py:57 calls civicos.history.search_decisions(state_manager=None, ...). When the explicit vector_backend returns no results AND _jurisdiction_has_embeddings(jurisdiction) is True for some other corpus but the per-corpus auto-detect ALSO returns empty for decisions, search_decisions falls through to line 1207 (`city_state = state_manager.get_city_state(jurisdiction)`) and crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_city_state'`. The verbs layer catches it per-corpus and emits a `Corpus decisions error` log line at WARN, but does NOT propagate the error to the response — the user just sees fewer results with no indication anything failed. Reproduced on city-tiburon (no vectors at all) and county-marin (105 decisions but 0 decision vectors) during the mass-ingest validation pass. Re-confirmed firing twice on 2026-04-07 evening validation run AFTER tiburon ingest — the bug is still active even with tiburon now having 8 decisions, so the trigger is some empty-vector path other than tiburon.
items.notes: Fixed 2026-04-09. Added defensive guard in search_decisions(): if state_manager is None and both vector paths returned empty, return [] instead of crashing. Also added missing error logging in the cross-jurisdiction run_corpus exception handler in verbs.py (was silently swallowing all exceptions). Regression test covers state_manager=None with empty explicit vectors, empty auto-detect, and unknown jurisdictions. validate_mass_ingest.py now produces zero Corpus decisions errors across all 15 jurisdictions.

items.description: Implement free YouTube auto-captions as an alternative transcription path to AssemblyAI. items.name: low_velocity_cron_timeout
items.priority_note_2026_04_19: Promoted from P1 to P0. Blocks re-extraction of the 474 decisions cleared by the BIGINT migration (those sit at NULL until next weekly cron completes). Also blocks freshness for school-marin-county-oe and school-ross-valley (both BoardDocs, last_verified 2026-04-09, cron crashed at school-marin-county-oe meeting 73/84). Priority raised to 0 as jurisdiction_qc_walkthrough completes.
items.description: Weekly scheduled_low_velocity_refresh cron on Modal is unreliable: 3 of the last 5 runs (2026-04-12, 2026-03-29, 2026-03-22) hit the 4h (14400s) Modal function timeout. Last failure crashed mid-way through school-marin-county-oe decision extraction at meeting [73/84], leaving all alphabetically-later jurisdictions (school-miller-creek through tamalpais, state-california) completely unprocessed for municipal code, agenda items, decisions, and legislation text population. The pipeline already wraps per-stage per-jurisdiction calls in try/except so soft failures are logged, but the hard Modal timeout kills the process entirely. Serial iteration over 31 jurisdictions is the core issue. Candidate fixes: (1) fan-out per-jurisdiction work via Modal .spawn() (existing pattern in this file, e.g. extract_decisions.spawn at line 6352) and collect with .get(), (2) shard the cron into multiple workflows by jurisdiction type (cities, schools, states) each with their own time slot, (3) add a time-budget checkpoint that skips jurisdictions already processed in the last N days so a failed run picks up where it left off on retry.
items.notes: Surfaced 2026-04-17 during city-berkeley QC parity check. Root cause confirmed via gh run view 24298312361 logs: FunctionTimeoutError at 14400s, last successful stage was school-marin-county-oe meeting [73/84] at 2026-04-12T08:06:29Z. Summary line: '56/73 passed, 17 stages failed' — the failures are late-alphabetical jurisdictions that never ran, not individual per-jurisdiction errors. Same session also fixed one contributor: fetch_municipal_code now guarded by data_sources.municipal_code gate in scheduled_low_velocity_refresh (was throwing ValueError every week for all jurisdictions without a Municode client). That reduces noise + wasted cycles but does not solve the serial-iteration time bound. Recommended structural fix is .spawn() fan-out. ~1-2 sessions. | 2026-04-19 PROGRESS: Spawn fan-out implemented + committed (commit 9fdb337a). scripts/modal_ingest.py now defines _refresh_jurisdiction_low_velocity (per-jurisdiction container) and scheduled_low_velocity_refresh spawns one per active jurisdiction, collects via .get(). Unit tests in TestLowVelocityCronFanOut pass. REMAINING: modal deploy + gh workflow run to verify end-to-end, then verify the 474 BIGINT-cleared decisions get non-NULL values. Keep status=not_started until verified in a live cron run. | 2026-04-19 UPDATE: Manually triggered cron run 24635788298 completed "success" in 1h 35m BUT against commit 8ce9eb9553 (April 16 state, serial code). Fan-out fix was NEVER deployed — my 2 fan-out commits (9fdb337a, 0531e911) plus 15 prior-session commits are unpushed on local main. GH Actions runs modal-run on the workflow-triggering commit (origin/main). The successful run this week was a lucky lighter workload, not a fix. To actually verify fan-out: git push origin main (needs user auth), then re-trigger workflow. Status stays not_started. | 2026-04-19 DONE: verified via GH Actions run 24637784320 against commit 2289cb7d. "Spawned 30 per-jurisdiction low-velocity refreshes in parallel" log confirms fan-out active. Completed in 41 min (vs 1h 35m serial-by-luck, vs 4h+ timeouts). Pipeline summary: 94/95 stages passed (1 lingering per-stage failure, not a timeout).

items.name: jurisdiction_qc_walkthrough
items.description: Manual jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction QC audit against live municipal websites. COMPLETED 2026-04-19. All 29 configured jurisdictions audited (15 cities/counties with content + 11 school districts + college-marin + county-sonoma + state-california). Uncovered and fixed 12 bugs: ProudCity P.M. regex, phantom version bloat from tz mismatch, CivicPlus AMID discovery, BoardDocs no date guard, Ross mixed-client stale rows + domain migration, Granicus Spanish Audio Files phantom rows, Granicus default_view_id skipped when archives configured, Berkeley Granicus archive keys non-semantic (view_2/view_5 stored as meeting_type), Postgres meeting upsert has_changes omitted meeting_type, scheduled_low_velocity_refresh called fetch_municipal_code unconditionally (now gated on data_sources.municipal_code), Granicus System Test streaming health-checks ingested as meetings (now skipped via _AUXILIARY_AUDIO_TITLES), pdf_parser.py 'closing' catch-all label misapplied to 36K chunks project-wide (now falls back to 'unparsed' + secondary numbered-bullet regex added for Alameda/SF/Berkeley-style agendas). Plus two systemic-data bug fixes applied to prod: BIGINT migration on decisions.financial_impact_cents (474 bogus INT32_MAX sentinel values cleared) and chunks.agenda_item closing->unparsed rename (36,611 rows).
items.notes: Started 2026-04-15. Next jurisdiction: school districts (11 of them; 8 known-Simbli-blocked per simbli_incapsula_bypass). Pattern: query DB, cross-reference with live website via WebFetch, flag config gaps and data quality issues. Each session should tackle 3-5 jurisdictions and fix any bugs surfaced. Document follow-ups: (1) universal.py:461-474 meeting_type inference is broken (produces null or title-cased snake_case); same bug also affects playwright_llm client per SF findings, (2) meeting disappearance detection not wired into refresh pipeline, (3) county-marin has 30 stale granicus-playwright-v1 rows with 11.8k chunks that duplicate active granicus.py rows — migration decision pending, (4) county-marin BOS meeting titles are yearly folder labels like 'Board of Supervisors 2025' with midnight timestamps because Marin's Granicus archive table uses year folders as Name column; fixing requires drilling into AgendaViewer pages, (5) SF has 44 stale playwright_llm meeting rows from 2026-04-06 onboarding (last refresh 2026-04-10) with 992 unique chunks + 222 decisions (177 unique) attached. playwright_llm produced inconsistent meeting_type variants (budget_and_finance vs budget_and_finance_committee, government_audit_oversight vs government_audit_and_oversight_committee) causing same-body-multiple-types clutter. Cleanup blocked: playwright_llm chunks have 0% content_hash overlap with granicus chunks (granicus never re-extracted them). Fix path: re-run chunk/decision extraction under granicus meeting_ids, then retire playwright_llm rows, (6) SF is missing 14+ advisory bodies not configured as Granicus archives (Assessment Appeals Board 1/2/3, Youth Commission, Sunshine Ordinance Task Force, LAFCO, SF Transportation Authority, Civic Engagement and Immigration Committee, various Joint City/School committees). Each needs a Granicus view_id discovery pass. (7) Berkeley is missing Rent Stabilization Board (view_9) which actively publishes through Apr 2026 — covered by expand_granicus_discovery. Berkeley also has upcoming-vs-past dedup gap: same meeting appears as both 'City Council Meeting' (stub from default view) and 'Regular City Council Meeting - 6:00 p.m.' (archived with video) because title_slug differs across the two states — meeting_id diverges and stubs never reconcile. Likely hits other Granicus jurisdictions configured with default_view_id overlapping per-body archives. (8) Berkeley's meeting_datetime values are all midnight; this is correct given Granicus date column shows date-only. Meeting time is embedded in the title (e.g., '... - 6:00 p.m.'). Extracting from title would need a separate pass. (9) Alameda: view_id=3 (CDA) is a multi-body archive covering Planning Commission, West/East County Boards of Zoning Adjustments, Castro Valley MAC - Land Use, Parks/Recreation/Historical Commission, Airport Land Use, Altamont Landfill, Agriculture Advisory, etc. All stored with meeting_type='community_development' which loses per-body distinction — search/filter by specific body is impossible. Same pattern as Berkeley's view_2/view_5. Could be addressed by expand_granicus_discovery splitting into per-body archives if each body has its own view_id, or by parsing body name from title. (10) Alameda: System Test rows (Apr 14, Apr 16) ingested as meetings — these are Granicus streaming health checks, not real meetings. Add 'System Test' to the _AUXILIARY_AUDIO_TITLES-style skip list in granicus.py (currently only skips 'Spanish Audio Files'). Pure data-quality fix, low-risk. (11) Alameda: a few [-A] rows (Health Committee - Cancelled Apr 13, Eden Area MAC Apr 14, Sunol Citizens Advisory Apr 15, Elections Commission Apr 16) appear in DB but not in live site's active archives — same cancelled-then-removed pattern as Berkeley Mar 26 ZAB. Needs the meeting-disappearance-detection follow-up (#2). (12) Local-only landmine found: data/extraction/county-alameda.json had been reverted in working tree to stale 'board: 1' config with stripped election_sources; restored this session. Prod was unaffected (Modal deploys from HEAD) but any local ingest would have failed. Worth adding a commit-hook or CI check that validates extraction JSONs against live Granicus view_id existence. (13) SYSTEMIC BUG: chunk.agenda_item='closing' and agenda_title='Closing Materials' is the dominant tag across EVERY jurisdiction: county-marin 27,448; city-berkeley 1,209; city-san-rafael 1,035; city-san-francisco 676; county-alameda 2,723. Root cause at packages/civicos/src/civicos/_internal/meetings/pdf_parser.py:218-223 in _parse_with_patterns: when AGENDA_ITEM_PATTERN regex does not match at all (or fails to match items beyond the first section), the final catch-all block labels every remaining chunk with item_number='closing', title='Closing Materials'. Alameda's Apr 7 Regular Meeting is a textbook example — 51 chunks spanning the entire agenda body, all labeled 'closing'. Breaks per-item semantic filtering (agenda_item parameter in history.py is effectively useless for these meetings). Fix requires broadening AGENDA_ITEM_PATTERN or pivoting to an LLM-based item-boundary detector for agendas that do not follow the expected numbering format. (14) SYSTEMIC BUG: decisions.financial_impact_cents column is INTEGER (INT32) in Postgres. Any amount above $21,474,836.47 overflows. 474 of 2,462 decisions with financial data (19.3%) have the INT32_MAX sentinel value of 2147483647 cents across 13 jurisdictions — county-alameda 213, city-san-francisco 142, school-ross-valley 29, city-berkeley 22, county-marin 16, etc. These are not real values; they are either direct overflow or a fallback sentinel when the extraction insert fails. Fix: ALTER COLUMN financial_impact_cents TYPE BIGINT, then re-run decision extraction for the affected rows. Consider also capping unreasonable LLM outputs (> $1B is almost certainly wrong for a single item). (15) Decision granularity: LLM collapses multi-sub-item agenda actions into single decisions (Alameda Apr 7 'Meal Service Contracts for Older Adults' is one DB decision but 7 distinct contract amendments in the agenda; 'Coliseum Negotiations' collapses 3 separate negotiating parties; closed session litigation with 5 case names absent). Not a launch blocker, but user-visible information loss. Needs a prompt-engineering pass in the decision extractor or a hierarchical decision schema.

items.description: Ingest candidate data for local races (city council, county supervisor, school board). The county registrar is the authoritative source — they publish candidate filings for all local offices. Marin registrar (marincounty.gov/depts/rv) has candidate filing pages. BoardDocs/Simbli could provide school board member names.
items.notes: Extracted local candidate data from Civera ElectionStats GraphQL API for all 3 pilot jurisdictions. Fixed extraction pipeline: skip empty elections, namespace election IDs by jurisdiction, broadened division filters to capture council districts. San Rafael: 21 contests/37 candidates (mayor, council D1-D4, clerk, measures). Mill Valley: 8 contests/26 candidates. San Anselmo: 11 contests/29 candidates. School districts deferred (cross-city boundary mapping needed).

items.name: ballot_measure_content
items.description: Ingest ballot measure text, fiscal impact summaries, and pro/con arguments. State measures come from the CA voter guide (voterguide.sos.ca.gov). Local measures come from county sample ballots. Currently we only store pass/fail results, not the measure content itself.
items.time_sensitive: 2026-06-02 CA primary — measures on the ballot need explanatory content
items.notes: Model extended with full_text, fiscal_impact fields. to_dict() serializes all content fields. CA voter guide client extracts from LAO (fiscal impact) and VIG (full text, pro/con args). Civera extraction includes content field placeholders. Explore my_ballot displays ballot_measure data for measure-type contests. VIG HTML blocked by Cloudflare; LAO is accessible. VIG HTML for 2026 primary available April 3, 2026.

items.name: election_deadlines_scraping
items.description: Scrape key election deadlines from CA SOS: voter registration deadline (15 days before), same-day registration availability, mail ballot send date, early voting start, ballot drop-off locations. Currently election_deadlines table exists but is unpopulated.
items.time_sensitive: 2026-06-02 CA primary — registration deadline ~2026-05-18, deadlines must be surfaceable before then
items.notes: Implemented via generate_ca_deadlines() — computes standard CA deadlines (VBM mailing, registration, early voting, conditional registration, election day) from Elections Code rules. Seeded for all pilot jurisdictions. Deadlines now appear in whats_next() responses. Completed as part of election_calendar session.
